sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the making of a dwelling place in the lower worlds requires both subjugation (itkafya) and transformation (it'hapcha) of the sitra achra, as the Zohar mentions only subjugation but the maamar adds transformation.

translations.translation: b)

And based on this, we can explain what is said in the maamar, that the making of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is through subjugation and transformation, as in the statement, "When the sitra achra is subjugated, the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated in all worlds."
For in the Zohar passage that it cites, it says, "When the sitra achra is subjugated," but in the maamar it says "subjugation and transformation."
And we can explain this:
For the Zohar passage speaks about drawing down a revelation from above
("the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated in all worlds" —
the drawing down of the encompassing light),
and this is accomplished through subjugation,
through a person acting against his nature and will
(as above, section 10),
but in order for there to be a dwelling place in the lower worlds —
for the concept of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is that the revelation drawn down into the lower worlds should also be from the perspective of the lower worlds themselves,
so that they become vessels for it
(as above, section b) —
this is accomplished through subjugation and transformation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that transformation (it'hapcha) brings a superiority of light from darkness itself, reaching a level beyond revelation and connecting to Atzmus, requiring both subjugation and transformation.

translations.translation: And we need to understand,
for it is explained in the maamar regarding the advantage of transformation,
that the superiority of light comes specifically from darkness,
for by darkness being turned into light, a superiority of light is produced.
From this it is understood
that the advantage of transformation is not only in relation to the lower being
(that through the work of transformation a vessel is made),
but rather that through transformation a superiority is also produced in the drawing down
(the superiority of light).
And in the Zohar passage that it cites, it says, "When the sitra achra is subjugated," etc.
And we can say,
that the drawing down through subjugation is a revelation,
but the revelation is beyond relation to the worlds.
[For by a person acting against his nature,
the drawing down of the revelation is not according to his nature,
and also the light that is beyond relation to the worlds
("is elevated")
is drawn down in revelation into the world.]
And the work of transformation reaches a place that is beyond revelation
[for that darkness is turned into light is from the perspective of Atzmus, to which light and darkness are equal.
And also,
because through transformation the lower being becomes a vessel
(as above),
through which the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is fulfilled —
the intention of Atzmus],
and through this a superiority is also produced in the light and revelation drawn down from there.
Therefore both aspects are needed,
subjugation and transformation,
for first there must be the drawing down of revelations through subjugation,
and through the transformation that follows subjugation,
the lower being becomes a vessel for the revelation,
and a superiority is also produced in the revelation, whose drawing down is from a place beyond revelation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that both subjugation and transformation are primarily found in the Baal Teshuvah, whose transformation comes from his own power, as hinted in the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on Dovid Hamelech.

translations.translation: c)
And behold, these two matters are primarily in the Baal Teshuvah.
For in addition to the Baal Teshuvah reading and reviewing more than his nature and habit, as brought above
(section 10)
from the discourses of the Admo"r Maharash,
the Baalei Teshuvah conquer their evil inclination more than the righteous.
And likewise regarding the work of transformation.
For the main advantage of transforming darkness into light is when the transformation of darkness into light is not from the side of the light, but rather the darkness itself is turned into light,
and this matter is primarily in the Baal Teshuvah.
For in the righteous,
even their work of transformation is through their feeling of G-dliness,
a revelation from above,
but the transformation of the Baal Teshuvah,
who changes and is transformed from one extreme to the other,
is from his own self.
And we can say,
that this matter is hinted at in the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov on the verse "And there was evening and there was morning," etc.
(brought above in section 7),
where he explains there
[in continuation of the explanation regarding the matter of "I do not know in which of them He delights"]
what Dovid Hamelech said,
"I considered my ways, and turned my feet to Your testimonies."
"I considered my ways" — that Dovid would think about his physical ways
(as explained there the reason for this),
"and turned my feet" — I will return to accustom
("feet" from the term "habit")
to Your testimonies.
And we can say,
that Dovid's matter is that he established the ascent of teshuvah.
And in the aforementioned teaching of the Baal Shem Tov, he hints at the two advantages of the Baal Teshuvah:
"I will return to accustom" — change of habit,
subjugation,
and the explanation of the matter of "I do not know in which of them He delights" — the matter of choice and work with his own power
(as above, section 7),
transformation.
